problem: Urban simulators are either hand-crafted (CARLA, ~15 scenes, not scalable) or procedurally generated from hard-coded templates (MetaUrban, UrbanSim) that deviate from real-world layouts and have few asset classes and no physics annotations. Navigation foundation models trained on passive, non-interactive data avoid neither obstacle-avoidance failures nor the lack of action-effect dynamics.
motivation: Data scaling only helps generalization if the data reflects the real-world distribution. City-tour videos on YouTube offer diverse real street layouts but have no actions or interactivity. Converting them into physics-aware simulation scenes would combine real-world diversity with the interactivity needed for RL on urban navigation.
key_idea: Convert uncalibrated city-tour videos into a scene graph (objects, ground, sky) and instantiate multiple 'digital cousin' IsaacSim scenes by retrieving metric-scale, physics-annotated assets from a 100K-asset urban database, then train RL navigation policies on them.
insight: Training layouts grounded in real-world video distributions produce power-law scaling of navigation generalization (error vs. number of layouts and of cousins per layout), whereas the same number of procedurally generated UrbanSim scenes barely improves. Full-length (~200 m) scenes beat half-length ones (SR 41.9 vs 32.3), and training directly on the test scenes overfits (SR 26.5), so diverse real-grounded scenes matter more than scene-specific training. A simple RGB-only PPO policy then beats large foundation models in the real world.
method: UrbanVerse-100K: 102,444 metric-scale GLB objects curated from Objaverse (human filtering of 800K down to 158K, CLIP categorization into a 659-class three-level ontology, GPT-4.1 annotation of 33 semantic/affordance/physical attributes such as mass and friction) plus 288 PBR ground materials and 306 HDRI skies.

Scene distillation: GPT-4.1 lists visible categories; MASt3R lifts the video to metric depth, intrinsics and poses; YOLO-World + SAM2 give instance masks that are fused across frames into object nodes (category, centroid, oriented box, yaw, crops); Mask2Former segments road and sidewalk; sky crops are taken from the upper half of each frame.

Materialization and diversification: for each object, CLIP category matching, then mBBD box-distortion filtering (top 1000), then DINOv2 appearance re-ranking to pick K=5 cousin assets; ground materials are picked by pixel MSE and HDRI skies by HSV histogram matching.

Simulation scene creation: fit ground planes (sidewalk raised 15 cm), texture them, light with the HDRI dome, place objects at their pose while avoiding penetration, assign physics parameters and enable rigid-body dynamics in UrbanSim/IsaacSim; ORCA-based dynamic agents (pedestrians, cars, scooters) can be added.

Scene library and benchmark: 32 YouTube videos (24 countries) x 5 cousins = 160 training scenes; a test benchmark of 10 auto-generated scenes from hold-out videos plus 10 artist-designed CraftBench scenes.

Policy learning: PPO with a small CNN on RGB (135x240) plus the goal-relative position, with arrival/collision/tracking/velocity rewards, trained on scenes rotated every 100 episodes; zero-shot deployment to a Coco wheeled robot and a Unitree Go2.

setting.backbone: Small CNN (3 conv layers) + MLP actor-critic trained with PPO from scratch; the scene pipeline uses frozen GPT-4.1, MASt3R, YOLO-World, SAM2, CLIP and DINOv2
setting.model_size: small CNN policy (exact parameter count not given)
setting.training_data: 160 UrbanVerse simulation scenes built from 32 YouTube city-tour videos; assets from 102K curated Objaverse objects
setting.observation: monocular RGB (135x240) + relative goal position from GPS waypoints every 5 m, no map
setting.action_space: continuous velocity commands (v, ω) for the wheeled robot / (vx, vy, ω) for the quadruped via a PD controller
setting.privileged: none at test time (goal relative position from GPS/odometry only)

results: PPO-UrbanVerse reaches 41.9 SR on CraftBench, +6.3 over the best baseline MBRA (35.6), and far above PPO-UrbanSim (9.1). In the real world it achieves 77.1 SR on the wheeled robot and 89.7 on the quadruped, beating S2E by +29.2 and +31.1 SR. It completes a 337 m mission with only two human interventions.
limitations: Tailored to street-level urban scenes; parks, campuses and indoor-outdoor transitions are not supported.
Reconstruction degrades under low light, fast motion or heavy occlusion, causing depth/pose drift and misplaced objects; asset appearance matching is imperfect (75.1% retrieval accuracy).
Only RGB goal-conditioned navigation with a simple PPO policy is evaluated, and the physical annotations come from GPT-4.1 (mass MAPE ~19.6%).
